attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No Yang-Mills estimate currently computes or bounds the connected reflected Wilson boundary OPE well enough to determine Phi_B, Phi_N, and the magnitudes a_{ij} for realized three-hairpin families.
steps: Start with regulated reflection positivity at fixed collar: every cutoff matrix N_{a,L}^{delta}=(S_{a,L}(\Theta F_i^delta,F_j^delta)) is positive.

Use RG convergence in the reflected-probe topology to pass a fixed-collar subsequence to a positive continuum collar matrix, then close the cone to obtain N^delta>=0 and finally N>=0 for the collar limit.

Use the prior trace analysis: diagonal trace continuity plus positivity eliminates positive additive contacts, so any remaining Wilson boundary discrepancy must be multiplicative on the finite matrix entries.
Write N=B\circ M. The intended same-theory target is therefore M=B^{[-1]}\circ N, not N itself.
For two observables, positivity of M gives only |N_{ij}/B_{ij}|<=1. This is valid but incomplete.
For three observables, normalize the diagonal and compute det M. The determinant contains the phase-sensitive term Re(q_{12}q_{23}\overline{q_{13}}), giving the phase-window inequality.
Algebraic model check: with B_{ii}=N_{ii}=1, B_{ij}=1/2, N_{12}=N_{23}=0.3, and N_{13}=-0.3, both B and N are positive and all pairwise thresholds pass, but det(B^{[-1]}\circ N)=-0.512.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite determinant criterion is valid mathematics, but the bridge still needs an analytic theorem that actual Balaban/RG Wilson collar limits satisfy it for all locked finite families. Without that, the criterion is only a sharp detector and not a proof of OS positivity.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: three-hairpin Schur-preimage obstruction

assumptions: At fixed positive collar, RG convergence is valid for every reflected quadratic form S(\Theta F_i^delta,F_j^delta), so the closed-cone argument gives N>=0.
Diagonal trace continuity is already secured; any positive additive boundary contact with zero diagonal vanishes by finite-dimensional Cauchy-Schwarz.
B is Hermitian with B_{ii}>0 and B_{ij} nonzero for the tested pairs; diagonal factors are absorbed by congruence so N_{ii}=B_{ii}=M_{ii}=1.
The three observables remain in the same locked gauge-invariant Wilson algebra before and after cutoff removal.
definitions: source object: a regulated lattice/RG family of reflection-positive gauge-invariant Schwinger forms evaluated on three collar-separated Wilson hairpin observables F_i^delta, with cutoff first removed at fixed collar and then delta down to 0 to produce a positive collar OS matrix N.
target object: the intended continuum OS matrix M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j) for the same uncollared Wilson observables in the physical gauge-invariant Schwinger theory.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, localized to the collar-collapse trace map N=B\circ M and the Schur-preimage test M=B^{[-1]}\circ N.

same-theory condition: the boundary factor B must be forced by the locked Wilson observable embedding and existing renormalizations; it may not add a new boundary Hilbert sector, pair-dependent counterterm, or coefficient-dependent change of test algebra.
B^{[-1]} denotes entrywise reciprocal on the tested finite matrix entries, not an operator inverse.

equations.label: multiplicative trace factor
equations.valid_when: Valid when collar collapse creates no additive contact and all remaining boundary renormalization is a nonzero pairwise multiplicative factor on this finite Wilson family.

equations.label: pairwise necessary threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid after diagonal normalization for each two-observable principal minor of the intended target matrix M.

equations.label: triple determinant obstruction
equations.valid_when: Valid for a normalized Hermitian 3 by 3 OS target matrix; this is the first phase-sensitive condition beyond pairwise damping.

equations.label: phase window
equations.valid_when: Valid when all a_{ij}>0, with Phi_N=arg(N_{12}N_{23}\overline{N_{13}}) and Phi_B=arg(B_{12}B_{23}\overline{B_{13}}); if some a_{ij}=0 the condition reduces to the pairwise minors.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a realized Wilson hairpin triple whose N and B are positive and pairwise thresholds are valid, but whose phase-window inequality fails; that finite determinant is a concrete falsifier of the same-theory continuum passage.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma sharpens the bridge from a two-by-two damping criterion to an exact three-observable same-theory OS test. It identifies the boundary cross-ratio phase as real Yang-Mills data, not a cosmetic normalization.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For three locked Wilson hairpin observables, fixed-collar reflection positivity gives a positive collar-limit OS matrix N. If collar collapse differs from the intended plane value only by a nonzero Hermitian multiplicative boundary factor B, then same-theory OS positivity for this triple is exactly positivity of M=B^{[-1]}\circ N. Pairwise damping |N_{ij}|<=|B_{ij}| is only necessary. The first complete phase-sensitive test is the normalized 3 by 3 determinant; a realized violation is a falsifier of the controlled interface even when every two-observable test is valid.

assumptions: The multiplicative relation N(F)=B(F)\circ M(F) holds on the chosen finite family.
B(F) has no zero entry on required pairings or else the test family is split before taking entrywise reciprocals.
The RG topology controls the collar matrix entries; the remaining unproved estimate is boundary trace control of B(F).
definitions: realized Wilson cone: the collection of finite matrices N(F) obtained as actual collar limits of reflected Wilson observables from the fixed test algebra.
boundary anomaly matrix: the finite Hermitian matrix B(F) encoding collar-to-plane multiplicative trace factors after diagonal congruences and after additive contacts have been ruled out.
Schur preimage: the entrywise quotient M(F)=B(F)^{[-1]}\circ N(F), which is the target OS matrix if the same-theory identification is valid.

equations.label: finite OS quadratic form
equations.valid_when: Valid for a finite locked Wilson family once the collar-to-plane discrepancy is purely multiplicative.

equations.label: finite bridge criterion
equations.valid_when: Valid as a finite-dimensional Hermitian matrix condition; the analytic burden is proving it for every realized Wilson family.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A single realized finite family with B^{[-1]}\circ N having a negative eigenvalue defeats the same-theory bridge, even if N itself is reflection-positive.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is the finite-dimensional form of the RG-to-OS passage after the formal closed-cone step. It prevents overclaiming from universal Schur multiplier arguments by restricting attention to realized Wilson matrices.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a finite locked Wilson family F_1,...,F_m with collar-limit matrix N(F) and multiplicative boundary anomaly B(F), the continuum OS form on that family is positive if and only if B(F)^{[-1]}\circ N(F)>=0. Therefore the bridge must prove Schur-preimage positivity on the realized Wilson cone, not on all abstract positive matrices and not merely on pairwise minors.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if an actual Wilson boundary OPE computation yields a realized triple with det(B^{[-1]}\circ N)<0; then the same-theory RG-to-OS route must be replaced by an OS-preserving construction or an explicitly boundary-renormalized theory.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves finite Schur-preimage positivity for a dense locked Wilson core, beginning with the three-hairpin phase-window inequality and extending to all finite reflected Wilson matrices.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a sharper finite determinant lemma and an algebraic falsifier model, so it is still learning rather than cycling on the closed-cone slogan.

dependency_updates.description: The bridge is no longer just closed-cone transfer plus pairwise boundary damping; it requires finite Schur-preimage positivity B^{[-1]}\circ N>=0 on realized Wilson matrices, with the three-hairpin determinant as the first nontrivial test.
The locked algebra must contain enough Wilson hairpin triples to test boundary cross-ratio phases; otherwise a nontrivial boundary sector could evade detection while changing the theory.

The topology must control reflected finite products through triple phases, not just individual entries or two-point thresholds. The required continuity is a finite-matrix trace topology for Wilson boundary OPE data.
A perturbative or constructive bound for B and N on triples sharing a reflection-plane footprint is now the decisive experiment for this branch.

falsifiers: A realized three-hairpin Wilson family with normalized B_{ij}=1/2, N_{12}=N_{23}=0.3, and N_{13}=-0.3: B and N are positive, pairwise thresholds are valid, yet det(B^{[-1]}\circ N)=-0.512, making it a finite-matrix falsifier of same-theory OS positivity.
A boundary OPE producing a cross-ratio phase Phi_B that pushes cos(Phi_N-Phi_B) below the phase-window bound while keeping |N_{ij}|<=|B_{ij}| for every pair.
Any cutoff-removal topology that controls N pairwise but not the triple reflected product phase; it can certify all two-by-two minors while missing an invalid 3 by 3 OS determinant.

A nonzero connected coincident-footprint Wilson boundary sector whose Gram factor is not absorbed by the locked observable renormalization and whose Schur preimage has a negative eigenvalue on a realized finite family.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 200 learned that the valid same-theory obstruction is phase-sensitive finite Schur-preimage positivity. Pairwise damping rho_N<=|B_{ij}| is necessary but can miss a negative 3 by 3 determinant. The concrete new invariant is the phase difference Phi_N-Phi_B in q_{12}q_{23}\overline{q_{13}}. Thus the next falsifier is not merely a nonrank-one boundary Gram factor; it is a realized Wilson triple whose boundary cross-ratio phase makes B^{[-1]}\circ N indefinite.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the small-loop or perturbative boundary OPE for three reflected Wilson hairpins with a shared reflection-plane footprint; extract B_{ij}, N_{ij}, Phi_B, and Phi_N, then test the normalized determinant det(B^{[-1]}\circ N) before returning to the general finite-matrix proof.
